analyses.content: 录音明确提到过去的机场候机区非常基础，它们更像是公共汽车站（bus station）。

So if we start by going back to, um, the nineteen sixties and seventies when there were a lot fewer airports than there are today, well, check-in desks, customs, and waiting areas were all very basic. They were rather like a bus station, uh, designed to allow air traffic in and out of the terminal, but not very welcoming for passengers.
你可能会听到“basic（基础）”或者“waiting areas（候机区）”，但这不符合题目中“把过去机场比作（compare to）”的逻辑对应。
But that all changed in the next few decades, and if you look at any big airport now, it's more like a mini city.
你可能知道“mini”对应“small”，但要注意直接提取其后的核心名词“city”作为答案。
录音中对比说到现在的任何大型机场，都更像是一个微型城市（mini city），对应题目中的“small”加名词。

The first was the huge increase in passenger numbers, in the number of people traveling by plane. And this was a direct result of mass tourism with things like, um, cheap holiday packages and low-cost airlines, with the construction of high-rise hotels and hotel complexes.
你可能会被后面跟着的一连串具体例子（holiday packages, low-cost airlines等）干扰，但只有“mass tourism”才是概括这些例子的根本原因。
录音解释乘客数量增加的一个直接原因是大众旅游（mass tourism），随后以便宜的度假套餐（holiday packages）作为举例。
And then people started traveling more regularly from one country to another for things like meetings, and so the growth in international business also pushed numbers up.
你可能光听到了“开会（meetings）”作为举例，但没往后听到能够总结人数增长原因的核心词“international business”。
录音提到人们为了开会（meetings）而在国家间往来，这导致国际商业（international business）的增长推高了人数。

The second reason for the change is, and this is a key aspect of airport design, people have realized that the airport is the first place you see when you visit another country. This means it forms your first impression of that country, and that impression has to be good.
你可能会听到“第一（first）”就急着找词，容易被前面的“地方（place）”干扰，但题目需要的是创造好的感受，即印象。
录音强调机场是你访问另一个国家看到的第一眼，这就形成了你的第一印象（first impression），而且这个印象必须是好的（good）。
录音先说到过去昏暗的机场被宽阔的开放区域（open areas）所取代，接着才用北京机场举例说那里有充足的空间和光线。

First, the dark enclosed airports of the past have been replaced by large open areas that look out onto the surroundings. Look at this picture of Beijing Airport. There's a huge amount of space and light, and this is typical of many airports today.
你可能是听到了题目里的“space and light（空间和光线）”后才去找词，这是典型的答案前置，需要你在听到举例后往前回溯。
People who want to feel calm and relaxed, who want to get around the airport easily. In this way, the stress of modern travel has been minimized.
你可能听到了前面的“calm（平静）”想找词填，但没有敏锐捕捉到题目中“减少（reduces）”对应的同义替换词“minimized”，导致跟丢答案。
录音说人们想在机场感觉平静和轻松走动，通过这种方式，现代旅行的压力（stress）就被最小化了（minimized，对应题干的reduces）。

Look at this picture of the Arctic Circle Airport in Norway. The airport itself is surrounded by mountains. So as you can see, the roof of the airport has been designed so that it's shaped like a range of mountains.
你可能会被“山脉（mountains）”这个词干扰，但题目问的是机场具体哪个部分的形状（the shape of the...），而不是像什么。
录音以挪威的机场为例，直接指出机场的屋顶（roof）被设计得形状像一排山脉。
In the same way, these airports in Thailand and India have beautiful shaded gardens all around them that reflect the landscape of the country.
你可能会听出后面的“风景（landscape）”一词，但填空限制在两个词以内且要符合空间位置关系，填入“shaded gardens”或“gardens”才准确。
录音顺着话题，直接提到在泰国和印度的这些机场周围有美丽的阴凉花园（shaded gardens）。

They're often light steel structures with what looks to the passenger like a lot of glass.But this is special glass that can maximize daylight and comfort and cut down on energy use.Bangkok's main airport is flooded with controlled daylight in a tropical climate, and this is achieved through the use of new materials and modern technology, which have also allowed engineers to come up with methods of reducing costs.
答案和costs中间跨越了较多内容，你容易在听到cut down on (减少) 时没有立刻锁定 energy use，等听到 costs 时再找已经来不及了。
录音提到特殊的玻璃可以减少能源使用（energy use），随后在下一句补充说这也让工程师想出了降低成本（costs）的方法。
